+++ b/src/click/strict_corrected_stream.py
@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import typing as t
+
+from ._compat import _is_compatible_text_stream
+from ._compat import _make_text_stream
+from ._compat import _stream_is_misconfigured
+
+
+def strict_corrected_stream(
+    text_stream: t.IO[t.Any],
+    encoding: str | None,
+    errors: str | None,
+    is_binary: t.Callable[[t.IO[t.Any], bool], bool],
+    find_binary: t.Callable[[t.IO[t.Any]], t.BinaryIO | None],
+    force_readable: bool = False,
+    force_writable: bool = False,
+) -> t.TextIO:
+    """Like :func:`click._compat._force_correct_text_stream`, but when
+    the stream must be rewrapped and ``errors`` is not given, decoding
+    and encoding errors are raised (``"strict"``) instead of replaced.
+    This suits data imports where silently corrupting input is worse
+    than failing.
+    """
+    if is_binary(text_stream, False):
+        binary_reader = t.cast(t.BinaryIO, text_stream)
+    else:
+        text_stream = t.cast(t.TextIO, text_stream)
+        # If the stream looks compatible, and won't default to a
+        # misconfigured ascii encoding, return it as-is.
+        if _is_compatible_text_stream(text_stream, encoding, errors) and not (
+            encoding is None and _stream_is_misconfigured(text_stream)
+        ):
+            return text_stream
+
+        # Otherwise, get the underlying binary reader.
+        possible_binary_reader = find_binary(text_stream)
+
+        # If that's not possible, use the original reader as-is.
+        if possible_binary_reader is None:
+            return text_stream
+
+        binary_reader = possible_binary_reader
+
+    # Default errors to strict so invalid data is reported, not replaced.
+    if errors is None:
+        errors = "strict"
+
+    # Wrap the binary stream in a text stream with the correct
+    # encoding parameters.
+    return _make_text_stream(
+        binary_reader,
+        encoding,
+        errors,
+        force_readable=force_readable,
+        force_writable=force_writable,
+    )
diff --git a/tests/test_strict_corrected_stream.py b/tests/test_strict_corrected_stream.py

index 0000000..edd2ea0
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_strict_corrected_stream.py
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+import io
+
+import pytest
+
+from click._compat import _find_binary_reader
+from click._compat import _force_correct_text_stream
+from click._compat import _is_binary_reader
+from click.strict_corrected_stream import strict_corrected_stream
+
+
+def _reader(stream, encoding=None, errors=None):
+    return strict_corrected_stream(
+        stream, encoding, errors, _is_binary_reader, _find_binary_reader
+    )
+
+
+def test_binary_defaults_to_strict():
+    stream = _reader(io.BytesIO(b"\xff"), encoding="utf-8")
+    assert stream.errors == "strict"
+
+    with pytest.raises(UnicodeDecodeError):
+        stream.read()
+
+
+def test_original_still_replaces():
+    stream = _force_correct_text_stream(
+        io.BytesIO(b"\xff"), "utf-8", None, _is_binary_reader, _find_binary_reader
+    )
+    assert stream.errors == "replace"
+    assert stream.read() == "\ufffd"
+
+
+def test_explicit_errors_respected():
+    stream = _reader(io.BytesIO(b"\xff"), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+    assert stream.read() == "\ufffd"
+
+
+def test_empty_input():
+    assert _reader(io.BytesIO(b""), encoding="utf-8").read() == ""
+
+
+def test_compatible_text_stream_returned_as_is():
+    text = io.TextIOWrapper(io.BytesIO(b"abc"), encoding="utf-8", errors="strict")
+    assert _reader(text, encoding="utf-8", errors="strict") is text
+
+
+def test_text_stream_without_binary_returned_as_is():
+    text = io.StringIO("abc")
+    assert _reader(text, encoding="latin-1") is text
